text:
nate: FYI — I'm scheduling a short 'privilege unwind' next week to reclaim stale admin/owner entitlements. Target: accounts with no activity in >180d. Will run in canary, then org-wide. :calendar:

sasha: 👍 can you drop the exact criteria? will need to surface service accounts + cross-account grants separately.

nate: Criteria draft:
- role IN ("org-admin", "project-owner", "kms-admin")
- last_active < now()-interval '180 days'
- no recent justification ticket in `#access-requests`

ashley: Also check `kms:Grant` events for service keys — some owners are only in KMS bindings, not IAM.

ajay: Agreed. We should run this query first (quick pg example):
```sql
SELECT principal, role, last_active, last_justified
FROM rbac_access_snapshot
WHERE last_active < now() - interval '180 days'
  AND role LIKE '%admin%';
```

ajay: I'll run a dry-run and post counts. planning a 50-user canary (low-risk projects) then rollback if we see errors.

audit-bot: automated-check: 42 principals matched (service: 11, human: 31). report uploaded: https://internal.redwood/logs/priv-unwind/dryrun-1839999999.csv :file_folder:

ashahon: (typo: sasha) — quick Q: how do we handle owners who are listed but rely on KMS grants via cross-account policies? removing IAM owner won't remove KMS binding.

ashafix: (clarify naming) — we should create a tag/label on infra resources as "pending-unwind" and run a KMS binding reconcile before any deletion. ops can automatically strip the label if bind exists.

devops-oncall: If you plan to revoke any service principals, add a 24h revert window and a runbook entry. I'll prep a rollback lambda that re-applies bindings from snapshot.

nate: Good call. Runbook outline in draft: action -> dry-run list -> canary revoke -> monitor (24h) -> confirm -> bulk revoke -> post-audit. Include contact list and escalation to oncall.

ash: For exceptions (legal, SOC), we'll require a formal justification doc and a 30d re-review cadence. mark exceptions as `exempt-unwind` label.

ajay: One more technical note: some tooling expects `owner` tag on repos for deploy. We'll create a mapping to fallback owners (team-managed) for 2 weeks during canary.

ash: Can we also add an audit hook to KMS logs to detect failed decrypts after revocations? want an early signal of breakage.

audit-bot: suggestion: add filter `eventName:Decrypt` with error != "SUCCESS" and alert threshold 5 failures within 10m. I can wire an alert.

ash: Perfect. :+1:

nate: Timeline: dry-run today, canary Monday 09:00 UTC, review Monday 16:00 UTC. I'll post the final dry-run CSV and the canary list.

devops-oncall: I'll standby for 08:50 UTC to watch metrics. if anything spikes, ping #release-war-room and I'll revert. :eyes:

ash: tagging legal (@ashley) for any compliance exclusions.

ashley: got it. I'll review exception list and post back by EOD.

nate: thanks all. leaving action items: ajay to post dry-run counts, ashley to validate exceptions, devops-oncall to prepare revert lambda, audit-bot to enable KMS-failure alert.

ajay: posted dry-run link and initial counts in thread: 42 principals, 11 service, 31 humans — details in CSV.

nate: closing loop — will update slack when canary starts. :lock:
